svg.title: A county of 100,000 residents is reviewing its diabetes data for the year. Staff have two counts: the number of residents newly diagnosed at any point during the year, and the number of residents living with a diagnosis of diabetes on 31 December. A public health nurse is asked which measure each count belongs to.
svg.desc: Incidence counts only new cases arising in a defined period and is the measure of the risk of developing the disease. Prevalence counts everyone who has it at a point in time, new and long-standing together, and is the measure of burden on the health system. An attack rate is an incidence proportion used for a short, sharp outbreak with a defined exposed group, which is the wrong shape for a chronic condition.
